test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 20 March, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Choose the option that is the correct direct form of the sentence.

She said, since it was evening, she had to go for a run.

options.text: She said, “It is evening I must ran.”
She said, “It is evening I might go for a run.”
She said, “It is evening I should go for a run.”
She said, “It is evening I must go for a run.”

solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"she had to go for a run"** indicates obligation.
 
• It is usually conveyed by the modal verb **"must"** in direct speech.
 
• So, in **direct speech**, it changes to "I must go for a run."

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is: *''She said, “It is evening I must go for a run.”*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** is incorrect because the past simple "ran" is not used with "must" - we use the base form of the verb, which is "run."
 
• **Option 2 **uses "might," which indicates possibility rather than obligation. Therefore, it is not a suitable choice here.
 
• **Option 3** uses "should," which indicates advice or suggestion. Although "should" might sometimes be used to indicate a kind of obligation, in this context "must" is a better fit because it more accurately reflects the speaker's sense of duty or obligation to go for a run.
